subject: Leadership briefing: success metrics, open risks & contracting runway
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@orionhealth.com>, Markus Patel <markus.patel@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership briefing: success metrics, open risks & contracting runway

Hi Sarah / Markus —

Thanks again for taking time today. This thread is a short leadership-facing recap so your execs and procurement have a single view of what we heard, the success metrics for the pilot, and the decisions that need to land to keep the timeline.

Quick summary of what we heard (pain -> outcome):
- Pain: Inconsistent inference latency and unpredictable unit costs across models in production.
- Impact: Slower feature rollout and a 30% overspend on peak inference costs last quarter.
- Desired outcome: Predictable sub-150ms p95 latency for named workloads, 40% reduction in per-token cost via batching/caching, and a rollout path that keeps PHI in a VPC/private deployment.

Proposed pilot success criteria (short):
1) Latency: p95 <= 150ms for our 512-token distributed chat workload across 5K daily active users.
2) Cost: >= 30% reduction in run-rate vs current baseline on equivalent load.
3) Security: Demonstrated private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logging enabled.
4) Quality: BLEU/ROUGE parity on validation prompts within 3% of current model outputs.

Open risks & mitigation we discussed:
- SOC 2 / compliance evidence: we need your SOC 2 checklist; we'll share our SOC 2 report and an engineering runbook for the private deployment.
- Data residency & retention policies: can confirm retention windows and KV cache deletion within the pilot scope.
- Procurement timeline: your procurement team indicated a May/June contracting window; legal redlines could push to July.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Markus: confirm procurement's target contract date and any non-negotiable Po terms (payment schedule, indemnity caps).
- Sarah: please share the pilot acceptance criteria and internal execs who need the briefing (name + title).
- Redwood: we'll send the SOC 2 evidence stub, a proposed MPA with redlines, and a one-page pilot SOW by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments (stubs): Orion-MVP-Success-Metrics.xlsx (pilot KPIs), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (requested fields), proposed-mpa-redlines.docx (initial redlines).

I'll follow up with a short one-pager tailored for the exec briefing that summarizes business outcomes and escalation lanes.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@orionhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Patel <markus.patel@orionhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership briefing: success metrics, open risks & contracting runway

Thanks Tessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot acceptance: our VP of Product (Lena Park) will sign off on the quality/latency metrics but Procurement needs a clear SOW and financial commitment before we can greenlight infra changes.
- Budget: we have a pilot budget allocated but the threshold for exec approval is $120k (total pilot spend). If the MPA includes a month-to-month ramp with a not-to-exceed, that will help Procurement.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence is table stakes; we also need to see network diagrams for private deployment (VPC peering, firewall rules).

I can get you the names for the exec briefing — Lena Park (VP Product), Daniel Ruiz (CISO), and Megan Cho (Head of Procurement).

I'll loop internal legal on the MPA once we see the proposed doc. For timelines, we are aiming to start the pilot in June if contracting is completed by mid-May.

Sarah
Director of Engineering, Orion Health

Sarah — thanks for the fast turnaround and for naming the execs. A few technical notes to address the network/retention and quality asks so Procurement & Security can pre-clear: 

- SOC2 & network diagrams: attaching a SOC2 evidence checklist and a high-level VPC topology diagram in the Drive link (see related_links). We will redact any customer-specific IP ranges in the public doc.
- Data retention / KV cache: for the pilot we recommend a 30-day KV cache TTL with explicit deletion on request; we can scope a 0-day TTL for sensitive routes.
- Private deployment options: Redwood Private supports a dedicated VPC peering model (managed control plane, customer-managed data plane) and an on-prem option if you prefer air-gapped. Both support KMS/HSM for key management.
- Pilot SOW: suggested milestones — week 0 onboarding & networking; week 1 baseline ingest & profiling; weeks 2–4 tuning + acceptance testing; week 5 exec readout.

I'll update the Orion-MVP-Success-Metrics.xlsx with baseline numbers from our prod sim and send the proposed SOW text in a separate Drive doc by lunchtime.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Tessa / Sarah — quick procurement note: 

- Timeline confirmed: procurement target to finalize terms by 2026-05-20 to support a June start. If legal redlines extend, we will re-evaluate but Procurement will prioritize a short-term pilot MPA rather than a long-term enterprise contract to avoid executive re-approval.
- Financial guardrails: we need an explicit not-to-exceed for the pilot (please add to the SOW). Payment terms: Net 30 is standard; we can consider Net 45 for the pilot with milestone invoicing.
- Legal & redlines: I've uploaded a single doc with Procurement's standard redlines (proposed-mpa-redlines.docx). Please have your legal team review and provide a marked-up MPA or a statement of exceptions by 2026-05-14 so we can keep the May 20 target.

Assigning a single commercial contact will speed review — who should our legal team loop in at Redwood?

Thanks,
Markus Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Orion Health
